notices.text: The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be sat upon by somebody important. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the noble quarters: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; every noble has suddenly remembered they are tired.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} sat upon by somebody important should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be set for dinner. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the dining hall: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; dinner will be served on it, and dinner will feel honoured.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} set for dinner should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be sat on. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the dining hall: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the queue to sit on it has its own chairs.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} sat on should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be slept in. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at a lucky dwarf's bedroom: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; whoever gets it will never be late for work again, or ever wake up.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} slept in should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be hung in a doorway. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the main hall: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it opens, it closes, and it does both beautifully.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} hung in a doorway should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be filled with somebody's belongings. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at a bedroom: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; belongings have never been stored so grandly.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} filled with somebody's belongings should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be used to display a soldier's kit. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the barracks: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the kit on it will look better than the soldier.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} used to display a soldier's kit should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be hung with the squad's weapons. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the barracks: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the weapons on it are standing up straighter.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} hung with the squad's weapons should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be kept ready for a funeral. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the tombs: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; nobody is in a hurry to try it.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} kept ready for a funeral should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be set up in the great hall. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the great hall: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it looks back at you, kindly.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} set up in the great hall should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be filled and stacked. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the stores: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it rolls straight and stands steady, which the haulers appreciate.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} filled and stacked should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be filled with goods. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the stockpile: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it holds things so neatly the haulers have started weeping.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} filled with goods should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be filled and carried. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the stores: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it carries anything without a single split seam.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} filled and carried should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be locked with something precious inside. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at a bedroom: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the lid closes with a very satisfying thunk.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} locked with something precious inside should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be raised at the tavern. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the tavern: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; every toast sounds better from it.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} raised at the tavern should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be raised at a feast. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the tavern: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; wine in it looks like a noble's dream.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} raised at a feast should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be placed on a noble head. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the treasury: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the nobles have started measuring their heads.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} placed on a noble head should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be slipped on a finger. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the treasury: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it fits any finger that the bookkeeper approves.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} slipped on a finger should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be fastened on a wrist. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the treasury: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it jingles just enough to be noticed.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} fastened on a wrist should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be presented to a noble. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the treasury: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it is said to bring luck, which is new for this fort.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} presented to a noble should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be carried at ceremonies. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the treasury: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the mayor has practised holding it in a mirror.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} carried at ceremonies should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be set on a shelf. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at a high shelf: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it is small enough to pocket and too good to.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} set on a shelf should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be carried into battle. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it sings when swung, the swordsdwarves say.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} carried into battle should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be swung at the enemy. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the axedwarves have begun drawing lots for it.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} swung at the enemy should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be levelled at the enemy. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it is long, sharp and very well behaved.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} levelled at the enemy should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be swung at goblin heads. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the macedwarves are humming happily.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} swung at goblin heads should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be swung in battle. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the hammerdwarves have formed a fan club.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} swung in battle should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be aimed from the walls. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the marksdwarves are already arguing over it.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} aimed from the walls should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn on the head. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; whoever wears it will have the best-protected thoughts in the fort.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn on the head should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn into battle. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it fits like it was waiting for its soldier.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn into battle should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be carried into the line. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the shield wall just got one good shield stronger.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} carried into the line should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn on a soldier's hand. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it grips a weapon like a promise.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn on a soldier's hand should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn on the march. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the soldier who wears it will march in comfort.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn on the march should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be strapped to a soldier's legs. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the armory: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the shins of the militia are safer for it.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} strapped to a soldier's legs should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn under everything else. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the clothing stockpile: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it is soft enough to wear all week, which somebody will.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn under everything else should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn against the cold. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the clothing stockpile: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it billows nicely in the corridor draughts.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn against the cold should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn every day. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the clothing stockpile: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the seams are perfect, which is rare in trousers.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn every day should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn on one foot. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the clothing stockpile: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it is the finest sock in the fort, and it has a partner somewhere.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn on one foot should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be worn against the wind. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the clothing stockpile: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the outdoor workers want one each.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} worn against the wind should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be served at dinner. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the dining hall: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the smell reached three levels up.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} served at dinner should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be eaten at breakfast. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the dining hall: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; they crunch in exactly the right way.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} eaten at breakfast should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be read in the library. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the library: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the scholars have stopped arguing to read it.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} read in the library should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be fitted into a lever or a trap. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the engineers' stores: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it clicks as sweetly as a cat purrs.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} fitted into a lever or a trap should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be used on a broken leg. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the hospital: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the doctor hopes nobody needs it, and is glad it's there.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} used on a broken leg should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be leaned on by the wounded. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the hospital: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it is so comfortable patients are reluctant to give it back.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} leaned on by the wounded should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be filled at the well. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the well: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it carries water without spilling a drop.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} filled at the well should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be set as a trap. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the trap corridor: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; it is ready for the next unwelcome visitor.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} set as a trap should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be played at the tavern. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the tavern: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the performers want to borrow it every night.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} played at the tavern should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be played at the tavern. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the tavern: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; its notes carry down every corridor.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} played at the tavern should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be beaten at the tavern. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the tavern: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the dancers keep time to it without trying.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} beaten at the tavern should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
The masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright} will be loosed at the enemy. Please do not borrow it first.
Now at the ammunition stockpile: the masterwork {masterwork} by {masterwright}. Admire it; the marksdwarves have promised to aim carefully.
Requests to have the masterwork {masterwork} loosed at the enemy should go to {masterwright}. Expect a long wait.
{fort} notes that the food stockpile is running thin. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the food stockpile is running thin.
Your Herald reports that the food stockpile is running thin; eat what you take and take only what you eat.
Remember: the food stockpile is running thin. And the cook has started counting plump helmets out loud.
The Overseer is aware that the food stockpile is running thin.
{fort} notes that the larder is in decent shape. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the larder is in decent shape.
Your Herald reports that the larder is in decent shape; keep the farms planted all the same.
Remember: the larder is in decent shape. And the cook has been seen smiling, briefly.
The Overseer is aware that the larder is in decent shape.
{fort} notes that there are more prepared meals than mouths. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: there are more prepared meals than mouths.
Your Herald reports that there are more prepared meals than mouths; share a meal with a friend.
Remember: there are more prepared meals than mouths. And the dining hall has run out of table, not food.
The Overseer is aware that there are more prepared meals than mouths.
{fort} notes that the drink stockpile is low. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the drink stockpile is low.
Your Herald reports that the drink stockpile is low; brewers to the stills, everyone else to the farms.
Remember: the drink stockpile is low. And the tavern keeper is pouring smaller mugs and hoping nobody notices.
The Overseer is aware that the drink stockpile is low.
{fort} notes that the cellar is well stocked. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the cellar is well stocked.
Your Herald reports that the cellar is well stocked; drink, but leave some for the haulers.
Remember: the cellar is well stocked. And the brewers have been granted an extra nap.
The Overseer is aware that the cellar is well stocked.
{fort} notes that the barrels are stacked to the ceiling. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the barrels are stacked to the ceiling.
Your Herald reports that the barrels are stacked to the ceiling; walk to the cellar before you get thirsty, not after.
Remember: the barrels are stacked to the ceiling. And the cellar now has a cellar.
The Overseer is aware that the barrels are stacked to the ceiling.
{fort} notes that there is no meat or fish in the stores. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: there is no meat or fish in the stores.
Your Herald reports that there is no meat or fish in the stores; the hunters and fishers are needed.
Remember: there is no meat or fish in the stores. And the butcher has taken up knitting.
The Overseer is aware that there is no meat or fish in the stores.
{fort} notes that there is meat and fish in the stores. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: there is meat and fish in the stores.
Your Herald reports that there is meat and fish in the stores; thank the hunters and the fishers.
Remember: there is meat and fish in the stores. And the cats have started visiting the kitchen hourly.
The Overseer is aware that there is meat and fish in the stores.
{fort} notes that there is not a single fish in the stores. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: there is not a single fish in the stores.
Your Herald reports that there is not a single fish in the stores; send a fisher to the water.
Remember: there is not a single fish in the stores. And the carp are said to be gloating.
The Overseer is aware that there is not a single fish in the stores.
{fort} notes that there are eggs in the stores. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: there are eggs in the stores.
Your Herald reports that there are eggs in the stores; thank a hen today.
Remember: there are eggs in the stores. And the hens have formed a union.
The Overseer is aware that there are eggs in the stores.
{fort} notes that it is raining outside. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: it is raining outside.
Your Herald reports that it is raining outside; keep below, or bring a hood.
Remember: it is raining outside. And the outdoor workers have discovered why dwarves live underground.
The Overseer is aware that it is raining outside.
{fort} notes that snow is falling outside. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: snow is falling outside.
Your Herald reports that snow is falling outside; keep the gate clear and the boots dry.
Remember: snow is falling outside. And the snow has been asked to leave and has declined.
The Overseer is aware that snow is falling outside.
{fort} notes that the sky is clear. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the sky is clear.
Your Herald reports that the sky is clear; if you must go up, go now.
Remember: the sky is clear. And the sky is still there, for those who check.
The Overseer is aware that the sky is clear.
{fort} notes that it is spring. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: it is spring.
Your Herald reports that it is spring; plant the fields and watch the gate for migrants.
Remember: it is spring. And the surface has turned green again, which upsets the miners.
The Overseer is aware that it is spring.
{fort} notes that it is summer. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: it is summer.
Your Herald reports that it is summer; harvest what is ripe and drink plenty.
Remember: it is summer. And the surface is hot and bright and nobody likes it.
The Overseer is aware that it is summer.
{fort} notes that it is autumn. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: it is autumn.
Your Herald reports that it is autumn; bring in the harvest and check the barrels.
Remember: it is autumn. And the trees are dropping their leaves, which is how trees apologise.
The Overseer is aware that it is autumn.
{fort} notes that it is winter. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: it is winter.
Your Herald reports that it is winter; keep the stores full and the fires lit.
Remember: it is winter. And the outdoor pond is now a floor.
The Overseer is aware that it is winter.
{fort} notes that the halls are crowded. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the halls are crowded.
Your Herald reports that the halls are crowded; be patient in the corridors.
Remember: the halls are crowded. And there is now a queue for the queue.
The Overseer is aware that the halls are crowded.
{fort} notes that the fort is small and everyone knows everyone. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort is small and everyone knows everyone.
Your Herald reports that the fort is small and everyone knows everyone; look after your neighbours, you have so few.
Remember: the fort is small and everyone knows everyone. And the roll call takes no time at all.
The Overseer is aware that the fort is small and everyone knows everyone.
{fort} notes that the fort is growing steadily. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort is growing steadily.
Your Herald reports that the fort is growing steadily; build bedrooms before they are needed.
Remember: the fort is growing steadily. And new faces outnumber old excuses.
The Overseer is aware that the fort is growing steadily.
{fort} notes that the fort is still young. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort is still young.
Your Herald reports that the fort is still young; dig deep and build the basics first.
Remember: the fort is still young. And the founders still argue about where the first stair went.
The Overseer is aware that the fort is still young.
{fort} notes that the fort has seen more than a year. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort has seen more than a year.
Your Herald reports that the fort has seen more than a year; tell the young ones the old stories.
Remember: the fort has seen more than a year. And the oldest corridor now has a name and a grudge.
The Overseer is aware that the fort has seen more than a year.
{fort} notes that the caverns are open below. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the caverns are open below.
Your Herald reports that the caverns are open below; keep the cavern doors shut at night.
Remember: the caverns are open below. And something down there keeps rearranging the mushrooms.
The Overseer is aware that the caverns are open below.
{fort} notes that the fort reaches very deep. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort reaches very deep.
Your Herald reports that the fort reaches very deep; mind the stairs on the way down.
Remember: the fort reaches very deep. And the deepest miners write home by bucket.
The Overseer is aware that the fort reaches very deep.
{fort} notes that merchants are at the depot. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: merchants are at the depot.
Your Herald reports that merchants are at the depot; bring your best goods and your hardest bargaining.
Remember: merchants are at the depot. And the merchants have noticed our mugs.
The Overseer is aware that merchants are at the depot.
{fort} notes that the depot is quiet. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the depot is quiet.
Your Herald reports that the depot is quiet; make goods now, so they are ready when the merchants come.
Remember: the depot is quiet. And the depot clerk is talking to the wagons that aren't there.
The Overseer is aware that the depot is quiet.
{fort} notes that the fort is at peace. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort is at peace.
Your Herald reports that the fort is at peace; train anyway; peace is a season, not a promise.
Remember: the fort is at peace. And the militia has been polishing things that are already shiny.
The Overseer is aware that the fort is at peace.
{fort} notes that the fort is at war with {enemy}. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort is at war with {enemy}.
Your Herald reports that the fort is at war with {enemy}; keep the gate guarded and the militia drilled.
Remember: the fort is at war with {enemy}. And {enemy} are said to read this paper, so the paper says the walls are very high.
The Overseer is aware that the fort is at war with {enemy}.
{fort} notes that the fort has a militia. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort has a militia.
Your Herald reports that the fort has a militia; feed the soldiers well.
Remember: the fort has a militia. And the barracks smell of polish and determination.
The Overseer is aware that the fort has a militia.
{fort} notes that the militia is large. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the militia is large.
Your Herald reports that the militia is large; keep them training in turns.
Remember: the militia is large. And the training yard needs its own training yard.
The Overseer is aware that the militia is large.
{fort} notes that the fort has no militia. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort has no militia.
Your Herald reports that the fort has no militia; raise a squad before you need one.
Remember: the fort has no militia. And the official defence plan is 'run'.
The Overseer is aware that the fort has no militia.
{fort} notes that the fort has a great many cats. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort has a great many cats.
Your Herald reports that the fort has a great many cats; watch where you step.
Remember: the fort has a great many cats. And the cats have begun holding meetings.
The Overseer is aware that the fort has a great many cats.
{fort} notes that the herds are large. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the herds are large.
Your Herald reports that the herds are large; keep the pastures in good order.
Remember: the herds are large. And the animals now outnumber the excuses for not shearing them.
The Overseer is aware that the herds are large.
{fort} notes that the fort keeps only a few animals. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the fort keeps only a few animals.
Your Herald reports that the fort keeps only a few animals; look after the ones we have.
Remember: the fort keeps only a few animals. And every animal has a name and an opinion.
The Overseer is aware that the fort keeps only a few animals.
{fort} notes that the gem stores are full. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the gem stores are full.
Your Herald reports that the gem stores are full; keep a few rough ones for strange moods.
Remember: the gem stores are full. And the jewelers have run out of shelf.
The Overseer is aware that the gem stores are full.
{fort} notes that metal bars are scarce. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: metal bars are scarce.
Your Herald reports that metal bars are scarce; send the smelters ore and fuel.
Remember: metal bars are scarce. And the smiths are hammering very carefully.
The Overseer is aware that metal bars are scarce.
{fort} notes that the bar stockpile is full. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: the bar stockpile is full.
Your Herald reports that the bar stockpile is full; let the smiths make something grand.
Remember: the bar stockpile is full. And the bookkeeper counts the bars twice for the pleasure of it.
The Overseer is aware that the bar stockpile is full.
{fort} notes that wood is scarce. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: wood is scarce.
Your Herald reports that wood is scarce; send the woodcutters out, carefully.
Remember: wood is scarce. And the carpenter is building very small things.
The Overseer is aware that wood is scarce.
{fort} notes that there is wood in the stores. Plan accordingly.
Fact of the week: there is wood in the stores.
Your Herald reports that there is wood in the stores; the carpenter is ready for orders.
Remember: there is wood in the stores. And the woodpile has been described as 'adequate', the highest praise for a woodpile.
